Article Title: Two memorials of 1962 war heroes figure in 27 places formally named in Arunachal
Article Text:
Havildar Shere Thapa of the 2nd Battalion, Jammu & Kashmir Rifles, was credited with saving the Subansiri Valley during the 1962 Chinese aggression

NEW DELHI: Sher-e-Thapa Memorial, set up in memory of 1962 China war hero Havildar Shere Thapa, is one of the 27 places in Arunachal that the Union government on Friday formally named by their standard names on the official Indian map.Havildar Shere Thapa of the 2nd Battalion, Jammu & Kashmir Rifles, was credited with saving the Subansiri Valley during the 1962 Chinese aggression. He was part of a team to delay the advance of the enemy. On Nov 18, 1962, undaunted by the advance of the Chinese troops, he continued to engage the enemy from his position despite his buddy succumbing to enemy action. The Chinese suffered heavy losses, and their advance was delayed by 72 hours. The Indian Army installed a memorial in his name.Another name, Jaswant Garh, which houses the memorial of Indian martyr Rifleman Jaswant Singh Rawat on Tawang Road, also figured in the list. Located at 10,000 feet on the highway to Tawang, it marks the site where he single-handedly fought Chinese forces for 72 hours during the 1962 war. The memorial has been built in honour of his extraordinary bravery at the Battle of Nuranang.Jairampur, an important logistics hub in Changlang district which is known as the gateway to the eastern border region supporting movements of security forces towards eastern Arunachal and the Myanmar frontier, also figures in the list.One of the most strategically important high-altitude passes, Thag La, where one of the opening battles between Indian and Chinese forces took place in 1962, has also been formally identified. The list also includes Bisa village and strategically important high-altitude mountain passes in the region: Dzo La, Riza La and Pukur La.By formally naming some of the places, famous for the memorials of the Army war heroes, the government is paying homage to bravehearts who laid down their lives fighting for India in the northeastern state.
Article Summary: Sher-e-Thapa Memorial, set up in memory of 1962 China war hero Havildar Shere Thapa, is one of the 27 places in Arunachal that the Union government on Friday formally named by their standard names on the official Indian map.

Article Title: India to recover 'Green Boots' climber's body from Everest after 30 years: Report
Article Text:
"Green Boots," the climber India is bringing home. Image Credits: Wikimedia Commons

The climber behind the ‘ Green Boots ’ mystery

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The body of an Indian climber believed to have become the mountaineering world’s infamous “Green Boots” could finally be brought down from Mount Everest, three decades after he died while descending from the summit.India is preparing a high-altitude recovery mission to retrieve the remains of Dorje Morup, an Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) personnel who died on Mount Everest in 1996, according to a detailed report by the BBC.Morup’s body has remained frozen at about 8,500 metres on the northern side of Everest for nearly 30 years. The remains became known among climbers as “Green Boots” because of the distinctive bright green mountaineering boots visible on the body.The ITBP is now looking for a specialist team capable of undertaking the difficult recovery operation. The force hopes to bring the remains back to India by September, after which DNA testing would be carried out to establish Morup’s identity conclusively, the BBC reported.If the identification is confirmed, his remains will be returned to his family in Ladakh.Morup was 48 when he joined a six-member ITBP expedition that attempted to climb Everest from the Chinese side in 1996.The expedition was seeking to become the first Indian team to reach the summit from that route.Three members of the expedition eventually turned back because of a snowstorm, while Morup and fellow climbers Tsewang Smanla and Tsewang Paljor continued towards the summit.All three reached the top, but disaster struck as they attempted to descend.A blizzard hit the mountain and killed the three climbers. Their bodies were left on Everest, as recovering bodies from the mountain is itself an extremely dangerous undertaking.For years, the body now known as “Green Boots” was assumed to belong to Paljor. However, surviving members of the 1996 expedition, along with information about the climbers’ final radio communications and the location of the body, have led authorities to believe that it was actually Morup.An ITBP official told BBC that Morup’s clothing and climbing equipment had also helped authorities identify the remains in recent years.The body has since become one of the most recognisable markers on the route to Everest’s summit, passed by climbers making their way through the mountain’s notorious “death zone”.For Morup’s family in Ladakh, the operation could finally resolve a mystery that has lasted three decades.His wife, Konchak Yangskit, told the BBC that she struggled to accept his death because she had never seen his body.Morup had told her before leaving for the expedition that he would return home after making the country proud. He had also asked her to look after their children and come to the airport to receive him when he returned.His son, Punchok Dorjai, told the BBC that the family plans to hold a funeral near Martyrs Park in Leh if the remains are confirmed as his.He also said the family intends to keep the green boots that gave Morup's remains their enduring identity on Everest.
Article Summary: Dorje Morup died on Mount Everest in 1996. His body has remained frozen at about 8,500 metres on the northern side of Everest for nearly 30 years. The remains became known among climbers as ‘Green Boots’ because of the distinctive bright green mountaineering boots visible on the body.

Article Title: “I'm going to kick his a**”: Austin Reaves throws a huge challenge to Lakers brother Luka Doncic in a candid joke
Article Text:
Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves. Image via: Joe Murphy/ NBAE via Getty Images

Luka Doncic's leadership and the Lakers' new-look roster

How Reaves and Doncic's numbers stack up entering 2026-27

Austin Reaves is already trash-talking Luka Doncic ahead of the Los Angeles Lakers' minicamp in Slovenia, and golf is the battlefield. Speaking at his 2026 Rigorer Basketball Camp, Reaves made clear he's arriving with a plan. "I'm going to kick his a** in golf," he said, before pivoting to the real point of the trip: getting a retooled Lakers roster comfortable with each other before training camp opens.The four-day camp, running Aug. 20 to Aug. 24, marks the first real gathering for a Lakers team that looks almost nothing like the one LeBron James left behind.Austin Reaves was in Hong Kong on his annual China tour when he was asked about the trip, and his answer doubled as both a joke and a mission statement. Golf has become his preferred way of getting under Luka Doncic's skin, and by his own account, it's one of the only competitions he's ever had a real shot at winning against his co-star.Doncic only picked up golf back in March, pushed into it by Reaves and James. He's a six-time All-Star coming off a scoring title and a fourth-place MVP finish, but a beginner with a driver in his hand. Reaves has reportedly beaten him at everything they've tried except basketball, which happens to be the one that decides games.The minicamp itself is Doncic's idea, and it says something about where he sees himself now that James is gone. He's hosting teammates in Ljubljana, mixing basketball workouts with sightseeing and golf, and using the week to fast-track chemistry a roster this reshaped badly needs. Doncic posted about the trip himself, writing that he's "looking forward to the time together" and excited to show his new teammates where he's from.The roster he's welcoming barely resembles last season's group. Walker Kessler, Quentin Grimes, Sandro Mamukelashvili, Collin Sexton, Kevon Looney, Ziaire Williams, Matisse Thybulle and Jaden Hardy are all new additions, brought in as general manager Rob Pelinka reshaped the team around Doncic's strengths. Rookie Cameron Carr is the only player who won't make it, held back by mandatory NBA rookie orientation.The two are now unquestionably the Lakers' core. Doncic averaged 33.5 points, 7.7 rebounds and 8.3 assists last season, numbers that carried Los Angeles even as the roster around him churned. Reaves backed that up with 23.3 points, 4.7 rebounds and 5.5 assists, production that earned him a four-year, $180 million contract this summer.That extension, paired with James' departure, settled any question about who the Lakers are building around. Head coach JJ Redick inherits a team with a clear top two and eight new faces still learning where they fit. A week in Slovenia, golf trash talk included, is Doncic's answer to how fast that gets figured out.
Article Summary: The Los Angeles Lakers are hosting a minicamp in Slovenia. Austin Reaves says he's going to "kick his a** in golf" Luka Doncic is hosting the camp, which is the first real gathering for the Lakers since LeBron James left.

Article Title: Why WNBA rescind Caitlin Clark’s one-game suspension? Here’s what we know
Article Text:
Caitlin Clark. Image via: Gary Dineen/ NBAE via Getty Images

WNBA reverses Caitlin Clark suspension decision after reviewing the incident

How the review process played out

Caitlin Clark's game performance and Fever's win over the Sky

The WNBA rescinded Caitlin Clark's one-game suspension hours after she picked up her eighth technical foul of the season on Saturday, Aug. 8, during Indiana's 90-86 win over the Chicago Sky. Clark drove along the baseline in the third quarter, lost the ball after contact from Chicago's Natasha Cloud, stumbled out of bounds, and ran into a referee, who whistled her for contact with an official.That technical would have forced Clark to sit out Tuesday's home game against Breanna Stewart and the New York Liberty. Instead, the league's reversal keeps her on the floor as the Fever try to string together back-to-back wins.The technical triggered an automatic one-game ban under WNBA rules, which suspend any player or coach who reaches eight technical fouls in a regular season. A person with direct knowledge of the league office's process, speaking to USA Today on condition of anonymity, confirmed the technical was rescinded. ESPN's Kareem Copeland also reported the reversal.Clark told ESPN's Holly Rowe afterward that she had already reviewed the play.“[The referee] said I ran into her. I’ve already watched it on the tape. So, we’ll let the league decide, but it wasn’t intentional or anything.So, I’m hoping it’s getting rescinded.”The contact drew a sharp reaction from Indiana's bench. Fever head coach Stephanie White picked up a technical of her own arguing the call, and officials reportedly told her Clark had intentionally sought out the referee and made forearm contact. White disagreed. "That's a bad call," she said, describing the contact as incidental given Clark was fighting to stay in bounds. " Incidental contact when you’re flying out of control. I thought her teammates should have come up and talked to her about that as well. I think that’s really bad. That s**t happens all the time in the game. You know, officials have to have some awareness in those moments, and it didn’t happen.”Had the suspension stood, Clark would have missed Tuesday's matchup with New York. Any Fever appeal would have needed league approval fast, since the next game was just three days out.The rescinded technical came in a game Clark played well. She finished with 26 points on efficient shooting, 11 assists, four rebounds, two steals and a block, bouncing back after a rough outing in Indiana's loss to Las Vegas the previous Thursday. Kelsey Mitchell led all scorers with 27 points, Aliyah Boston recorded a double-double with two blocks, and the Fever outscored Chicago 46-0 in paint points as a team.Indiana improved to 20-12 and now turns to New York, sitting at 19-13, for Tuesday's game in Indianapolis. With her technical wiped clean, Clark will be on the floor as the Fever look to extend their winning streak against a Liberty team that's chasing them in the standings.
Article Summary: Caitlin Clark picked up her eighth technical foul of the season on Saturday, Aug. 8, during Indiana's 90-86 win over the Chicago Sky. The technical triggered an automatic one-game ban under WNBA rules, which suspend any player or coach who reaches eight technical fouls in a regular season. A person with direct knowledge of the league office's process confirmed the technical was rescinded.

Where the Schroder trade market stands

Dennis Schroder's stay in Cleveland may be nearing its end. The Cavaliers are exploring multiple trade avenues involving the veteran guard as they work to open up financial flexibility for a run at free agents Jonathan Kuminga and Peyton Watson, according to Chris Fedor of Cleveland.com. Schroder split the 2025-26 season between Sacramento and Cleveland, landing with the Cavs ahead of February's trade deadline and averaging 10.8 points, 4.9 assists and 2.7 rebounds across 70 total games between the two stops.Moving his salary would help Cleveland chase Kuminga, whose $24.3 million team option was declined by Atlanta, and Watson, a restricted free agent whose rights still sit with Denver. The Hornets have previously shown interest in Schroder, and there is now talk that a trade involving him could take shape as the Cavs' pursuit of both forwards heats up.Schroder enters the final stretch of a contract that already has Cleveland thinking ahead. He turned in a solid two-stop 2025-26 season, splitting time between Sacramento and the Cavaliers after a February trade sent him east, and settled into a steady backup point guard role once he arrived.That steadiness is exactly what makes him movable. Cleveland has other options behind the starting backcourt, and Schroder's money is more useful to the front office as leverage right now than as a roster piece.The move isn't built around a return package so much as clearing the runway. Cavaliers sources tell Cleveland.com the front office is testing trade packages centered on Schroder specifically to gain financial flexibility aimed at free agents Jonathan Kuminga and Peyton Watson.Kuminga became an unrestricted free agent once Atlanta declined his $24.3 million team option, and he's coming off a season where he averaged 12.3 points on strong efficiency in just 16 Hawks appearances. Watson remains a restricted free agent whose rights sit with Denver, which likely means any Cleveland pursuit would require a sign-and-trade rather than a straight signing. Trimming Schroder's number is the mechanism that makes chasing either one realistic.There's no roster or draft package on the table here, since the Cavs aren't trading for either forward. What they're offering is opportunity: real minutes at forward, a rotation with a frontcourt hole left by Dean Wade's departure to Philadelphia, and cap room created by moving off Schroder's salary.Kuminga fits that gap directly. He's a 22-year-old forward who can play up a position, which lines up with what Cleveland has been missing since Wade left. Watson's fit isn't detailed in the brief beyond his restricted free agent status and Denver's hold on his rights, so what Cleveland would specifically offer him stays speculative until more is known.Freeing up Schroder's roughly $14.81 million average salary is the whole point of this exercise. That number, even if the two source instances disagree on the contract's total value, is real breathing room for a team trying to make a run at two frontcourt free agents at once.It also solves a roster problem beyond cap math. Cleveland is light at forward after Wade's exit, which is part of why it already added Mario Hezonja and why Kuminga and Watson, both capable of playing up a spot, are appealing beyond just their price tags.The clearest lead in the brief is Charlotte. The Hornets have previously shown interest in Schroder, though nothing in the reporting confirms active talks or a package being discussed between the two sides right now.Beyond Charlotte, the picture is thin. Schroder was previously floated as a possible salary piece in a LeBron James pursuit, but the current reporting frames him as someone Cleveland wants off the books, not someone with a confirmed destination yet.
Article Summary: Cleveland Cavaliers are exploring multiple trade avenues involving Dennis Schroder. The Cavs are looking to open up financial flexibility for a run at free agents Jonathan Kuminga and Peyton Watson. Charlotte Hornets have previously shown interest in Schroder, though nothing has been confirmed.

Article Title: Cristiano Ronaldo-Georgina Rodriguez wedding: Mystery deepens as unusual security measures reportedly emerge across Madeira
Article Text:

Funchal is on edge. Floors locked off. Bar areas shut down. Security perimeters quietly going up around one of the island's most famous five-star hotels. Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez have not said a word publicly, but Madeira is speaking for them. Reports from British and Portuguese media point firmly to August 8 as the day the world's most watched footballer marries his long-term partner in the city where he was born. Funchal Cathedral has been named as the ceremony venue. The Savoy Palace Hotel, roughly one kilometre away, is reportedly where the celebrations continue. Nothing confirmed. But everything pointing in the same direction.The Savoy Palace does not close floors for nothing. The five-star property in Funchal, overlooking the Atlantic, is already a destination in its own right: six pools, a spa, the sky-level Galaxia rooftop restaurant, and a Grand Ballroom that fits up to 1,000 people. Yet hotel guests have reportedly been notified that two full floors and several bar areas will remain off-limits on Friday and Saturday due to a private event. That kind of lockdown at a functioning luxury hotel is not routine.The Savoy Palace also houses "The Reserve" on its upper floors. Think hotel-within-a-hotel: a private rooftop infinity pool, exclusive dining, personal butler service and, crucially, a level of separation from regular guests that someone with Ronaldo's profile demands.Reports suggest Ronaldo and his family have already been spotted at the property ahead of the weekend. If the venue and the man are both in Funchal right now, the speculation stops being speculation very quickly.Funchal Cathedral adds the other piece of the picture. Local reports claim the 16th-century landmark, a Manueline architectural gem with one of Portugal's most admired cedar wood ceilings, has been reserved for a major wedding ceremony from 3 pm on Saturday. The cathedral is barely a five-minute drive from the Savoy Palace. No official confirmation has come from either the church or Ronaldo's camp, but the proximity of the two reported bookings, on the same date, in the same city, is difficult to read as coincidence.Names like Jennifer Lopez and Kylian Mbappe have appeared in circulation, though neither attendance has been confirmed. What is known is that this wedding, if it proceeds as reported, will not be small. The Grand Ballroom at the Savoy Palace can accommodate up to 1,000 guests. That number suggests a gathering built for more than close family. The scale of the security measures reinforces it.Ronaldo and Georgina have been together since 2016. He proposed in August 2025, nine years into the relationship. In his own words: "After so many years together, I felt it was the right moment to take this important step." Choosing Madeira to make it official carries real weight. This is the island where Ronaldo grew up. Funchal Cathedral stands a short distance from the hospital where he was born. Returning here for his wedding is a deliberately personal choice from a man who has lived most of his life in a fishbowl.Earlier speculation placed the wedding at the Quinta da Regaleira estate in Sintra. That was ruled out due to public access constraints. Madeira, specifically Funchal, offers what Sintra could not: a controlled environment, deep personal meaning, and a local infrastructure that knows how to handle its most famous son.The island has had years of practice.Ronaldo and Georgina have given no official confirmation. No statement, no social post, nothing. But the silence itself has become part of the story. Two hotel floors locked. A cathedral block-booked. A security perimeter going up around one of the most recognisable addresses in the Portuguese Atlantic. Whatever happens in Funchal this Saturday, Madeira is ready for it.

Article Title: NBA rumor: Lakers eye 6-foot-7 ex-Warrior free agent for an apparent frustrating role
Article Text:

Lakers are actively pursuing Jonathan Kuminga

Jonathan Kuminga. Image via: Getty Images

What are insiders saying about this?

Why Jonathan Kuminga's potential Lakers role could be frustrating?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Jonathan Kuminga's free agency has stretched past a month with no resolution, and the Los Angeles Lakers remain in the picture as a possible sign-and-trade destination. The 23-year-old forward, whose $24.3 million team option was declined by the Atlanta Hawks, is reportedly seeking $14-16 million annually, well above the roughly $10 million the Lakers initially floated.Both sides face structural hurdles. The Hawks have 16 players on guaranteed deals and only $3.8 million of tax room to work with, while the Lakers are hard-capped at the first apron following the Walker Kessler sign-and-trade, leaving them $8.1 million below that line. Talks have stalled for weeks even as ex- warriors star Kuminga's earning power shrinks with each passing week of free agency.The Lakers met with Kuminga early in free agency and pitched him on a significant role for a fringe contender that needs athletic wing depth. He was reportedly receptive to the idea, but the specifics of a sign-and-trade package sent back to Atlanta haven't satisfied both sides. The Kings and Timberwolves have also been floated as landing spots, and more recently the Timberwolves and Cavaliers have been mentioned as potential competition for the Lakers.Kuminga split last season between Golden State and Atlanta, averaging 12.2 points on 46.3 percent shooting, 5.6 rebounds and 2.3 assists across 36 games.The Lakers have already added wing depth this offseason through the draft and free agency, signing Mattise Thybulle and Ziaire Williams and drafting Cameron Carr, but the roster still lacks a downhill scoring option on the wing.ESPN's Anthony Slater has tracked the standoff closely. He reported that "the Lakers remain interested in him, league sources said", even as the two sides have failed to bridge the gap on years and money in a potential sign-and-trade. Slater's reporting frames this as Kuminga's second straight prolonged free agency process, with the Lakers' pitch appealing to the player but the financial terms proving to be the sticking point.Separately, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints reported in late July that Kuminga's camp was prepared to wait out the market rather than accept less than his target range. That posture cuts both ways: it signals confidence in his value, but it also means the clock is working against him as rosters fill out and free-agent dollars dry up elsewhere in the league.The cautionary tale sits on the Lakers' own roster departures. Rui Hachimura, dealt out this summer and now with the Clippers, spent last season boxed into a 3-and-D role next to Luka Doncic, LeBron James and Austin Reaves. He excelled there in the playoffs, shooting at a historic clip from three, but his comments since leaving suggest he wasn't satisfied playing that way. Speaking about his new team, Hachimura said the Clippers coaching staff wants him "to shoot my three-pointers, of course, but also do more cutting", and that he wants to get back to rebounding and pushing the pace, the kind of two-way game he says the Lakers' system didn't allow.That distinction matters because Kuminga isn't the same type of player Hachimura is. Hachimura could at least lean on catch-and-shoot volume to make a corner role work. Kuminga doesn't have that same track record as a floor-spacer. Writing for LakeShowLife.com, Maxwell Ogden argued that Kuminga lacks that specific skill set or skill level needed to thrive as a stand-and-wait shooter, and that his game is built around downhill attacks, transition finishing and pick-and-roll reps rather than standing in the corner.Ogden's point cuts to the core of the fit question: if Hachimura struggled with limited touches despite being suited to that exact role, a player less equipped for it could struggle even more.The absence of a rim-pressure creator like James running point could theoretically open a different pathway for Kuminga than the one Hachimura navigated, since someone would need to occupy that downhill space. But there's no indication yet that the Lakers' offense, as currently built around Doncic, would hand Kuminga the same frequency of drive-and-finish opportunities he'd want. Until a deal gets done and he's actually on the floor in that system, the fit question remains theoretical, and Hachimura's exit interview stands as the clearest data point the Lakers have generated so far on how their role players fare in that offense.For now, Kuminga remains unsigned, the sign-and-trade framework remains unresolved, and the Lakers remain one of several teams still in the conversation. Nothing here gets settled until a contract gets signed.
Article Summary: Jonathan Kuminga's free agency has stretched past a month with no resolution. The 23-year-old forward, whose $24.3 million team option was declined by the Atlanta Hawks, is reportedly seeking $14-16 million annually. Both sides face structural hurdles. The Hawks have 16 players on guaranteed deals and only $3.8 million of tax room.

Andre Agassi became one of tennis’ biggest stars despite saying he hated the sport he played for most of his life. The eight-time Grand Slam champion and 1996 Olympic gold medallist was pushed into tennis by his father, Mike Agassi, when he was very young. His childhood training included a powerful ball machine he called “The Dragon”, which sent balls at about 110 mph. Agassi later wrote in his autobiographyabout the fear, pressure and anger he carried from those years. Yet he went on to become world No. 1, complete a career Grand Slam and build a new purpose through education.For Andre Agassi, tennis was never simply a childhood game. His father, Mike Agassi, wanted one of his children to become a great tennis player and pushed Andre harder than most young players could imagine.Mike had been an Olympic boxer for Iran and brought the same strong approach to training. He built a tennis court at the family home in Las Vegas and made Andre spend long hours hitting balls. The young player was expected to keep going even when he was tired or wanted to stop.The most memorable part of that training was “The Dragon”, a modified ball machine that Mike made more powerful. It could send tennis balls towards Andre at about 110 mph., quoting Agassi’s account in, described how frightening the machine was for the seven-year-old.Agassi later explained his father’s thinking in“My father says that if I hit 2,500 balls a day, I’ll hit 17,500 balls a week, and at the end of one year I’ll have hit nearly one million balls. He says numbers don’t lie. A child who hits one million balls a year will be invincible.”For Mike, the numbers meant progress. For Andre, the endless practice became a source of fear and frustration. He was becoming better at tennis, but he was not developing a love for it.That conflict stayed with him for years. In, Agassi put his feelings into one of the most famous lines from the book:“I play tennis for a living even though I hate tennis, hate it with a dark and secret passion and always have.”The words were striking because they came from a player who would eventually become one of the most successful men in the history of the sport.By the time Andre Agassi reached his teenage years, tennis had already shaped almost every part of his life. At 13, he was sent to Nick Bollettieri’s tennis academy in Florida, where he trained alongside other young players hoping to reach the professional tour. The ATP Tour confirms that Agassi was sent to the academy at that age and turned professional at 16 in 1986.His appearance soon made him stand out. Long hair, bright clothes and a rebellious image made Agassi look like someone who wanted to challenge the traditional image of tennis.But there was a reason that rebellion mattered so much to him.For years, other people had decided what his life should look like. His father decided how much he should train. Tennis decided where he would travel. Coaches decided how he should play. The teenager’s loud style gave him a way to show that there was still a part of his life he could control.The pressure did not disappear after he became a professional. In fact, Agassi later said he had taken his father’s voice and expectations into his own mind.“I’ve internalized my father-his impatience, his perfectionism, his rage. I no longer need my father to torture me. From this day on, I can do it all by myself.”That pressure existed alongside major success. Agassi won his first Grand Slam at Wimbledon in 1992, followed by the US Open in 1994 and the Australian Open in 1995. He also won Olympic singles gold in Atlanta in 1996. By the end of his career, he had collected eight Grand Slam singles titles. Olympedia lists his eight major titles and Olympic gold medal.Still, winning did not automatically make him happy.Agassi’s career later reached a point where the champion everyone knew seemed to be disappearing. In November 1997, his ranking dropped to No. 141. Just two years earlier, he had been world No. 1.The fall was not only about rankings. Agassi had lost his direction and needed to decide whether he still wanted to keep playing.Instead of walking away, he started again at a much lower level. He played Challenger events, where the crowds were smaller and the conditions were far removed from the big stages where he had once been a star.The ATP Tour describes that period as the beginning of his comeback. After reaching No. 141, Agassi finished 1997 by playing Challenger events and then climbed back to No. 6 in 1998.The biggest moment of that comeback came at the 1999 French Open.Agassi won at Roland Garros and completed the career Grand Slam, meaning he had now won all four major singles tournaments. His list already included Wimbledon, the US Open and the Australian Open. The French Open was the missing piece.Winning it changed how his career was viewed. He was no longer simply the talented player with the flashy clothes and huge personality. He had shown that he could fall a long way and still find a way back.That comeback also gave Agassi a different relationship with tennis. He was no longer simply following the path his father had created for him. He had gone through the worst part of his career and chosen to continue.Away from the court, Agassi eventually found another part of his life that mattered to him deeply: education.He established the Andre Agassi Foundation for Education and later launched the Andre Agassi College Preparatory Academy in Las Vegas. The ATP Tour says the school opened in 2001 as a public K-12 charter school serving at-risk young people in his hometown.Agassi’s work with children gave his success a purpose beyond tennis. Instead of using his name only to celebrate what he had achieved, he used it to help young people get opportunities he felt he had missed.His personal life also changed. He married Steffi Graf in 2001. Graf is one of the greatest women’s tennis players ever, with 22 Grand Slam singles titles. Together, Agassi and Graf have continued to support education and charitable work.That change in outlook is reflected in another line from Agassi’s“It’s no accident, I think, that tennis uses the language of life. Advantage, service, fault, break, love, the basic elements of tennis are those of everyday existence, because every match is a life in miniature.”There is a clear link between that thought and Agassi’s own journey. His life had its advantages and faults, its wins and losses, and one major comeback after another.The boy who once wanted to escape tennis eventually became one of its greatest champions. But his story is not simply about learning to love the sport.It is about taking control of a life that had been planned for him.Andre Agassi did not choose tennis as a child. His father chose it for him. Yet after years of pressure, success, failure and a dramatic comeback, Agassi found ways to decide what tennis would mean to him.He finished his career with eight Grand Slam titles, an Olympic gold medal and a career Grand Slam. But his work in education became another important part of what he left behind.His story is inspiring because the difficult beginning did not have to decide the ending. Agassi turned the sport that once represented pressure into a platform for achievement and helping others. That shift, more than any single trophy, explains why his story still carries meaning.
Article Summary: The eight-time Grand Slam champion was pushed into tennis by his father. His childhood training included a powerful ball machine he called ‘The Dragon’ Agassi later wrote in his autobiography about the fear, pressure and anger he carried from those years. Yet he went on to become world No. 1, complete a career Grand Slam and build a new purpose through education.

Both superstars have parlayed their success in the ring into substantial personal wealth outside of it through contracts, endorsements, merchandise and outside business ventures.Roman Reigns may be the highest-paid active performer in WWE right now, but Brock Lesnar’s net worth includes more than just wrestling, having made a lot of money from UFC and some smart investments outside of the ring. He is said to make a multi-million dollar base salary, bonuses for appearances, merchandise revenue, payments for licensing and other incentives tied to major premium live events.Reigns has also kept his profile high commercially outside of WWE. Endorsement deals with worldwide companies like Nike, C4 Energy and Shady Rays are said to add another $1 million to $2 million per year. Add endorsement income and growing media opportunities into that mix and Roman Reigns looks to be well on his way to building his wealth for years to come.Brock Lesnar’s Pay cheque Extends Well Beyond WWE. Before becoming one of the biggest draws in pro wrestling, Lesnar established himself as a force to be reckoned with in mixed martial arts, winning the UFC Heavyweight Championship. He has been able to earn premium paydays across multiple sports, allowing him to build one of the strongest financial portfolios in combat sports.Unlike full-time WWE performers, Lesnar has been working under special-attraction deals for most of the past decade. Roman Reigns and Brock Lesnar built fortunes differently, combining wrestling success, endorsements, UFC earnings and investments.

Article Title: MrBeast dragged into fresh TeamWater controversy as Adin Ross demands receipts for $40 million fundraiser
Article Text:
Why Adin Ross wants a TeamWater audit

What Adin Ross said about MrBeast and Ray

Adin Ross has reignited questions surrounding MrBeast’s TeamWater campaign after challenging the YouTube star to provide a detailed account of how the reported $40 million raised was spent. The Kick streamer says he will apologise if a full audit and receipts show the funds were properly used. His comments came after MrBeast shared an update on the campaign’s progress.The dispute began after MrBeast posted a one-year update about TeamWater, a campaign created to help expand access to clean drinking water. MrBeast directly tagged Adin Ross and encouraged him to watch the update during a livestream.Ross did exactly that, but instead of simply praising the results, he questioned whether the visible progress matched the amount of money raised.“If $40 million was raised, why is there only one well? I’m expecting a f***** water park.”His comment quickly shifted the conversation toward transparency. Ross said he wanted to see a full breakdown of the campaign’s finances rather than rely only on a progress video.“Let’s do an audit. Chat, you know you will never do it. Let’s do an audit. Let’s see where all the 40 million went. Show receipts and do a full audit.”The streamer also made his position clear: he is not claiming that the money was definitely mishandled.Instead, he wants evidence showing where the funds went and what was achieved with them.That distinction matters because large charity campaigns often involve more than the final projects people can see. Funds may cover construction, equipment, logistics, staffing, administration and other costs. A detailed financial report would therefore provide more context than a single visual update.Ross went as far as offering to publicly admit he was wrong if the records satisfy his concerns.“If you do an audit, I will apologize.”He also said he would be pleased if the money had genuinely reached its intended purpose.“If everyone’s happy with this, I’m happy. All right? Seriously, I’m happy that this is what we got out of this.”Ross also questioned why MrBeast appeared to single him out when sharing the TeamWater update. He brought up streamer Ray, also known as RayAsianBoy, who had previously raised questions about the campaign.Ross argued that Ray deserved the same response and attention if he had also asked about the fundraiser.“MrBeast, you didn’t tag Ray. Ray asked as well. You didn’t tag anybody. You only tagged me.”The disagreement adds another layer to the already complicated relationship between Ross and MrBeast. Their public tension has previously included Ross claiming he was left out of MrBeast’s $1 million video.Ross also said his experience had changed how he views future charity streams, suggesting that he would prefer campaigns he joins to be based in the United States.“Any charity stream that I ever do again, it needs to be done in America.”For now, Ross has framed his challenge around transparency rather than a definitive accusation of wrongdoing. Whether MrBeast responds with a detailed audit could determine whether the controversy fades or becomes a much larger debate about online fundraising and accountability.

WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert has asked teams to prepare for more discussion about transgender athlete participation in women’s basketball, calling the issue one that needs a careful and respectful approach. Her memo comes as the league faces fresh questions after former NBA players Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White said they plan to enter the 2027 WNBA Draft. The debate also grew after Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham spoke about protecting women’s sports. Engelbert said team presidents and general managers will discuss the matter at a meeting next week, while the WNBPA has also spoken about inclusion. CAccording to The Associated Press, Engelbert sent the memo to WNBA teams on Friday after the recent attention around transgender participation.She wrote, “I know many of you have received questions in recent weeks regarding transgender athlete participation in women’s basketball, and I expect this topic will continue to receive significant attention.”Engelbert said in the memo obtained by The Associated Press. “I wanted to reach out to share how we are approaching these conversations at the league office and to thank those of you who have responded to questions from the media with thoughtfulness and professionalism.”Engelbert also said the league will discuss the matter with team presidents and general managers next week. She wrote that the WNBA will “always approach this topic thoughtfully, respectfully, and in alignment with the longstanding values of our league. … Preserving the integrity of our game and ensuring fair competition will always remain among the league’s highest priorities.”The memo followed announcements from Freedom and White about the 2027 WNBA Draft. Freedom said he had reviewed the league’s current eligibility rules and was declaring himself a WNBA prospect. White later said he would also enter the draft and said he identifies as transgender.Freedom said, “After careful consideration and reviewing the current eligibility guidelines, I’m officially declaring myself a WNBA prospect,” before arguing that the rules should apply equally to everyone. The WNBA’s collective bargaining agreement says that “only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA.”The latest debate follows comments from Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham in an ESPN profile published July 21. Cunningham said she had received criticism over her views but rejected the idea that she was attacking transgender people.“I got a lot of negative feedback about me hating trans. And I’m like, ‘I never once said that,’” Cunningham said. “I think that I am here to extend love. But I also think with that love is truth, being honest. And I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn’t have to go against biological men.”Cunningham added, “I’m very much in the middle. I agree with things on both sides, disagree with things on both sides. And that’s all I’ve ever said about my political beliefs. But people love to assume.”The WNBPA responded after Freedom’s announcement by stressing its support for different views and inclusion.The union said its members have different experiences, cultures and opinions, while adding that “Hate, abuse, and demonization of any person or group of people, including transgender people, only fuel fear, division, and harm.” It also said, “We will continue to have hard conversations. But we will not be used as political pawns.”
Article Summary: WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert has asked teams to prepare for more discussion about transgender athlete participation in women’s basketball. Her memo comes as the league faces fresh questions after former NBA players Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White said they plan to enter the 2027 WNBA Draft. Engelbert said team presidents and general managers will discuss the matter at a meeting next week.

A San Francisco father says he was warned he could face a $192 fine after park rangers questioned him while playing tennis with his two children at Golden Gate Heights Park. Sam Dogen said he was practicing with his six-year-old daughter and nine-year-old son when the rangers asked if he had a permit to teach tennis. He was not cited, and the exchange ended after one child confirmed Dogen was their father. The incident has raised a simple question for the family: where does coaching your own children cross into instruction that needs a permit?Dogen told Fox News that he had taken his children out for an afternoon of tennis and was feeding them balls as they practiced. The courts were empty when the rangers came over, about 20 minutes after the family started playing.“It’s just a situational awareness thing,” he said. “I’m not making a racket; there’s not a lot of noise, there’s nobody waiting, and it was just a surprise to me,” he said.According to Dogen, one ranger told him he could face a $192 fine for teaching tennis without a permit. San Francisco rules require permits for tennis instruction, while the Recreation and Parks Department says the rule is meant to stop people from offering lessons without approval.Dogen said the rangers were not accusing him of running a paid lesson. Still, he questioned why the family’s afternoon had to be interrupted when the court was not being used by anyone else.San Francisco Recreation and Parks spokesperson Tamara Aparton told the San Francisco Standard that the encounter was “a routine interaction.” She said rangers sometimes ask questions to work out whether someone is giving commercial instruction or simply “coaching their kids.”The department’s current tennis rules say lessons on its courts must be given by licensed instructors. Its court reservation rules also say reservations are for individual play and cannot be used for lessons, team practices, clinics or league matches. The department currently offers a system for booking lessons with licensed instructors at selected parks. The department says licensed instructors have exclusive access to dedicated instructional hours on select courts, while regular court bookings are for individual play.Dogen said he does not plan to apply for a permit to teach his children. Instead, he joked that he may carry their birth certificates when they play, so he can show that he is their father.“I don’t think I’m gonna be applying for a permit to teach my children. I think the property taxes I pay and being a good citizen should be good enough to use the public parks,” he said.Dogen was not cited during the encounter, and there is no indication in the account that he was fined. The issue, as described by the department, is whether someone is providing commercial instruction rather than simply helping their own children learn the game.
Article Summary: Sam Dogen was playing tennis with his two children at Golden Gate Heights Park. Park rangers came over and asked if he had a permit to teach tennis. Dogen says he was warned he could face a $192 fine for teaching tennis without a permit.

Article Title: Kanter and White WNBA eligibility: What the league rules say about their 2027 Draft plans
Article Text:
Kanter and White WNBA eligibility: What the league rules say about their 2027 Draft plans

Enes Kanter Freedom declares for the 2027 WNBA Draft

Royce White follows Enes Kanter Freedom into the 2027 WNBA Draft

What the WNBA rules say about eligibility

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Enes Kanter Freedom has declared himself a prospect for the 2027 WNBA Draft, saying the league’s rules on identity and inclusion allow him to do so. Soon after, former NBA player Royce White announced that he also plans to enter the draft and said he identifies as transgender. Their statements have brought new attention to the WNBA’s eligibility rules, especially what the league’s current rules actually say about who can enter the draft.Enes Kanter Freedom shared a video on X while wearing a WNBA hoodie. He said he had reviewed the league’s eligibility rules with his team before making the announcement.“After careful consideration and reviewing the current eligibility guidelines, I’m officially declaring myself a WNBA prospect,” Enes Kanter Freedom said.He added, “If simply declaring who you are is all that’s required, then I meet every single requirement necessary to compete in the WNBA.”Enes Kanter Freedom also said his team had looked at the WNBA’s rules on self-identification and inclusion. He stressed that he was not trying to mock or disrespect anyone. Instead, he said he wanted the rules to be applied equally.The former NBA center played for the Utah Jazz, Oklahoma City Thunder, New York Knicks, Portland Trail Blazers and Boston Celtics during his NBA career before retiring in 2022.Royce White soon made a similar announcement. The former Houston Rockets first-round pick, selected No. 16 overall in 2012, said he plans to enter the 2027 WNBA Draft and identifies as transgender for professional basketball.Royce White said he wants the WNBA to clearly explain its position on transgender athletes. He also said he expects to be treated fairly if he seeks entry into the league. His announcement came shortly after Enes Kanter Freedom’s post, linking the two statements directly.The current WNBA Collective Bargaining Agreement does not say that self-identification by itself makes a player eligible. Article XIII states, “Only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA.”The same section also lists separate draft requirements, including age and college-related conditions. The public CBA does not provide a detailed transgender eligibility process or say that declaring an identity alone is enough to qualify for the draft.That makes the key issue less about whether Enes Kanter Freedom or Royce White can simply declare for the draft and more about how the WNBA would apply its eligibility rules to either player.The debate follows recent comments from Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham about transgender athletes in women’s sports. The WNBPA later said it supports “justice, equity, diversity and inclusion” and added that it would not be used as “political pawns.”
Article Summary: Former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom declares himself a prospect for the 2027 WNBA Draft. Former NBA player Royce White says he also plans to enter the draft and said he identifies as transgender. Their statements have brought new attention to the WNBA’s eligibility rules.

Article Title: DS Penske reveal special golden retro livery for London E-Prix farewell

Championship-winning years with DS Techeetah

DS Penske have unveiled a special retro livery for the London E-Prix, their final appearance in Formula E. DS first partnered with Virgin Racing, now Envision Racing, during the Gen1 era. Jean-Eric Vergne and Sam Bird helped the team finish third in the championship standings.ID@undefinedCaption not available.ID@undefinedCaption not available.The biggest success for DS came during the Gen2 era after joining forces with Techeetah from Season 5. The team won two Formula E world championships. Jean-Eric Vergne claimed the title in the 2018-19 season, while Antonio Felix da Costa won the shortened 2019-20 campaign.Da Costa's 2020 title remains the biggest championship-winning margin in Formula E history. Healing Politics: A Doctor's Journey into the Heart of Our Political Epidemic

The Michigan Daily

Article Title: Who was Sydney Towle? TikTok star who inspired millions while documenting her cancer journey dies at 26
Article Text:
TikTok creator Sydney Towle has died at 26 after a nearly three-year battle with cholangiocarcinoma, a rare bile duct cancer. Known for documenting her cancer journey with honesty and optimism, she inspired millions by promoting awareness and self-advocacy. Her family confirmed her passing, while fans and celebrities, including Alyssa Milano, paid heartfelt tributes. Towle's resilience, positivity and determination left a lasting impact on countless people around the world.

Who was Sydney Towle before TikTok knew her story?

The diagnosis that changed everything

Why Sydney Towle chose to share her cancer journey

The online criticism she faced

How her followers responded after her death

Why Sydney Towle's story resonated with young people

Sydney Towle spent nearly three years showing the internet what courage looked like. Even as an aggressive cancer reshaped her life, the 26-year-old creator refused to let it define her spirit. Her death has left millions grieving, but the messages pouring across social media make one thing clear. Her honesty, optimism and determination created a legacy that will outlive every viral video she ever posted.Before becoming a familiar face on TikTok, Sydney Towle was a young woman with big ambitions and an infectious personality. Living in New York City, she loved fashion, spending time with friends and documenting everyday moments that felt authentic rather than curated. Her content reflected joy long before cancer entered the picture.As her online audience grew to more than one million followers on TikTok and over 200,000 on Instagram, people connected with her openness and warm personality. Even after receiving a life-changing diagnosis, she continued to celebrate milestones.One of her proudest moments came when she fulfilled a longtime dream by walking the runway during The Chemo Club x Post Swim show at Miami Swim Week.It became a powerful reminder that illness did not erase her dreams.Towle was diagnosed with cholangiocarcinoma, a rare and aggressive bile duct cancer. Over time, the disease spread to other areas of her body, including her peritoneum, the membrane surrounding the abdominal and pelvic organs.She underwent years of chemotherapy and numerous treatments while documenting both the victories and setbacks. In May, she revealed that her oncologist had stopped treating her cancer and recommended end-of-life care. Rather than giving up, she sought another specialist and remained determined to keep fighting.Her family announced her passing in a heartfelt message."Syd went peacefully last night after an almost three-year-long battle with cholangiocarcinoma."They also honored the purpose she found through her platform."We are so proud of how hard Sydney fought and for sharing her journey with so many people. She wanted to raise awareness for rare cancers and was passionate about promoting self-advocacy. We will continue her legacy and honour her in every way we can."Towle never hid the difficult realities of cancer. She showed hospital stays, treatment days, emotional lows and joyful moments with equal honesty.She even embraced the scars left by treatment, including the hepatic artery pump implanted in her body. Instead of hiding it, she used it to encourage others struggling with body image and illness.Her social media often balanced painful updates with hope."Rich in life because my friends choose to spend a Saturday fundraising for cancer research."She also reminded followers to appreciate life's simple pleasures."Go get a pint of Ben and Jerry's, watch your favourite movie, remember that life is good and bad things happen sometimes but that doesn't make it a bad life."In another deeply personal reflection, she wrote:"I have only recently started seeing the resilience and beauty in this body. Scars that remind me of how far I've come. And I'm reminded that dreams only end when you allow them to."Being transparent online also exposed Towle to criticism. Some questioned her appearance, while others misunderstood why she continued posting during treatment.She rarely allowed negativity to shape her message. Instead, she focused on educating people about rare cancers, encouraging early medical attention and reminding others that every patient's experience is different. Her content remained centered on hope rather than conflict, earning admiration for its honesty and resilience.The announcement of Towle's death prompted an overwhelming response across social media. Thousands shared tributes celebrating the impact she had on their lives.Actress Alyssa Milano wrote:"Sweet angel. Fly high. Praying for all who loved her. She is really something special."Other followers echoed the same feelings."You were such a bright light and will be missed."Another tribute read:"How lucky we all are to have found you on the internet. Thank you for sharing yourself and your story."The messages reflected how deeply strangers had connected with someone they had never met in person.Sydney Towle's influence stretched beyond social media numbers. She gave young adults facing illness someone who understood their fears without pretending everything was perfect. She spoke honestly about pain while still making room for laughter, friendship and hope.Her videos became more than updates. They became reminders that resilience can exist alongside vulnerability. By sharing every chapter of her journey, Towle transformed personal hardship into a source of comfort for countless people, ensuring her voice will continue inspiring others long after her final post.
Article Summary: Sydney Towle was diagnosed with cholangiocarcinoma, a rare and aggressive bile duct cancer. Her death has left millions grieving, but the messages pouring across social media make one thing clear. Her honesty, optimism and determination created a legacy that will outlive every viral video.

Article Title: Meet Betty Bromage: 97-year-old breaks her own Guinness World Record as oldest female wing walker after recovering from stroke
Article Text:
Meet Betty Bromage: 97-year-old breaks her own Guinness World Record as oldest female wing walker after recovering from stroke

Wing walk comes after recovering from stroke

'I'd just get bored otherwise'

Inspired by a message from her nursing days

Already planning a challenge for her 100th birthday

At an age when most people slow down, 97-year-old Betty Bromage has once again taken to the skies, this time to break her own Guinness World Record as the oldest female wing walker.The Cheltenham resident completed the daring challenge by being strapped to the top of an aircraft as it flew through the sky, raising money for the stroke unit at Cheltenham General Hospital, where she received treatment after suffering a stroke in 2025.The feat marks Bromage's sixth wing walk, with her first completed at the age of 87. She had previously set the Guinness World Record four years ago and has now reclaimed the title by surpassing her own achievement.Bromage suffered a stroke in 2025, which continues to affect her speech, but she said she was determined not to let it stop her from doing what she loves."They treated me so well," she told BCC, referring to the hospital staff who cared for her. "It affects my words, but the rest of me is fine."Her latest wing walk was organised to raise funds for the hospital's stroke unit as a way of thanking the medical team that helped her during her recovery.According to the hospital's charity, donations from the fundraiser will help purchase equipment that will benefit both patients and healthcare staff.Despite approaching her 100th birthday, Bromage says she has no plans to give up adventurous challenges."I'd just get bored of life otherwise," she said. "I can't drive, I can't see very well and I get a bit frustrated. So, I want to do the things I can do."Known for her fearless spirit, Bromage joked that the most difficult part of wing walking isn't flying through the air, it's climbing onto the aircraft."The only problem is getting up on the wing because I'm quite short. Once you're up there, no problem. The fairground is a lot worse," she said with a laugh.A former nurse, Bromage said her passion for fundraising was inspired by a quote she once saw displayed on a hospital wall."We pass through this world but once. Any good we can do, any kindness we can show, do it now. Do not defer or neglect it. You will not pass this way again," she recalled.She said those words have stayed with her throughout her life and continue to motivate her charitable work.Hospital charity representative Imogen Sims praised Bromage's extraordinary determination, saying staff were grateful for her support."To take on such a daring challenge to support our team is amazing," Sims said, adding that the funds raised would make a real difference for patients and staff alike.As for what's next, Bromage is already thinking ahead."I'll have to think of something when I'm 100," she said. "Something special."Her latest record-breaking wing walk has once again proven that age is no barrier to adventure, or to giving back to the community.
Article Summary: Betty Bromage, 97, breaks her own Guinness World Record as oldest female wing walker. Cheltenham resident completed the challenge by being strapped to the top of an aircraft as it flew through the sky. Bromage suffered a stroke in 2025, which continues to affect her speech, but she said she was determined not to let it stop her from doing what she loves.

Article Title: 18-year-old swept away in SE Delhi drain while returning from work, search operation underway

An 18-year-old youth slipped and fell into a drain before being swept away by a strong current of water in southeast Delhi’s Sarita Vihar Friday evening, triggering a search and rescue operation. He has not been traced so far, police said.The teen has been identified as Ankit, a resident of Bhim Colony in Ali village. Ankit, who worked as a pantry worker in Noida, was the elder of two siblings and returning home from work at the time of the incident.According to police, two PCR calls were received at 8.31 pm and 8.54 pm at the Kalindi Kunj and Sarita Vihar police stations, respectively, reporting that a youth had been swept away in a drain around 8 pm near the Priyanka Camp drain in Madanpur Khadar.Police teams rushed to the spot and met Manish, 23, a friend of Ankit. Article Title: 4 held for theft of 17 kg silver mask, cladding of Shivling at historic temple in Maharashtra's Khopoli
Article Text:
Khopoli police arrested four burglars for stealing silver items from a historic temple





NAVI MUMBAI: The Khopoli police in Raigad detected the burglary at the 18th century historic Shree Vireshwar temple, where 17 kg silver mask and silver cladding on Shivling was stolen on July 19 past midnight around 2 am, by arresting four accused burglars on Tuesday.The arrested accused are Amol Kasbe (36) and Vikas Agiwale (25), who were arrested from Shirur, Pune district and Dilip Jadhav (40) and Sakharam Gaikwad (40), who were arrested from Parner in Ahilyanagar district.The 17 kg silver mask and cladding on the Shivling was adorned in 2023 for which the around Rs 28 lakhs expenses were borne by the temple's trust from the donations received from devotees.Sachin Hire, senior inspector of Khopoli said, "On July 19, the assistant priest at the temple identified as Kishore Shigwan (56) lodge a complaint that the silver mask and cladding on Shivling was stolen. The thieves had entered the temple by breaking the chain and lock of the rear gate, which always remained close as the devotees were allowed entry only from the front gate.""Upon checking CCTV camera footage at the temple, it was seen that four masked men had entered the sanctum sanctorum around 2 am and decamped with the silver mask and cladding on the Shivling. Subsequently, an FIR was registered under BNS sections for house tres-pass, theft in a dwelling house and joint criminal liability. "Inspector Hire said, "Multiple teams were formed to trace the gang of burglars.Using technical expertise and informer network, we zeroed-in on four history-sheeters. They were traced to Pune and Ahilyanagar district and gradually apprehended on Tuesday.""They have revealed the place where they have hidden the stolen silver mask and cladding. Accordingly, a police team will recover the stolen valuables. Previously, there are criminal cases of theft and robbery registered against the arrested accused in Ahilyanagar and Pune districts."
Article Summary: The 17 kg silver mask and cladding on the Shivling was adorned in 2023 for which the around Rs 28 lakhs expenses were borne by the temple's trust. The arrested accused are Amol Kasbe, Vikas Agiwale, Dilip Jadhav and Sakharam Gaikwad.
